title: Understanding AI Models, Tools, and Applications
introduction: This lesson explains the difference between an AI model, an AI tool, and an AI application, and shows how a model becomes a useful product for everyday people.

sections.heading: AI Model
sections.subheading: The core algorithm that learns from data
paragraphs: An AI model is a mathematical representation that has been trained on data to recognize patterns or make predictions.
It does not have a user interface; it is just the learned knowledge that can be used by other software.

example.title: Example: Language Model
example.content: GPT‑4 is an AI model that has learned from billions of text examples. It can generate text when given a prompt, but by itself it cannot be used directly by a person.

sections.heading: AI Tool
sections.subheading: Software that applies a model to a specific task
paragraphs: An AI tool is a program that connects an AI model to a user‑friendly interface, allowing people to perform a task.
The tool handles input, sends it to the model, and shows the output in a useful way.

example.title: Example: Grammar Checker
example.content: Grammarly uses a language model to check your writing and suggest corrections. The model does the analysis, while Grammarly provides the interface and workflow.

sections.heading: AI Application
sections.subheading: A complete product built around tools and models
paragraphs: An AI application combines one or more AI tools, data pipelines, and user interfaces into a full solution that solves a real problem.
It may include many features beyond the AI part, such as storage, security, and integration with other services.

example.title: Example: AI‑Powered Photo Editor
example.content: Adobe Photoshop’s “Neural Filters” use image‑generation models, but the whole Photoshop program, menus, and file handling make it an AI application.

sections.heading: From Model to Product
sections.subheading: Steps that turn a model into a usable application
paragraphs: First, developers train or obtain a model. Next, they wrap it with code that handles inputs, outputs, and errors. Then they design a user interface or API so people can interact with it. Finally, they add data management, security, and deployment.
Each layer adds value, turning a raw model into a product that ordinary users can use without understanding the underlying math.

example.title: Example: Smartphone Face Unlock
example.content: A face‑recognition model learns to identify faces. The phone’s operating system adds a camera interface, security checks, and settings, creating the complete face‑unlock feature that users tap to open.

practice.title: Classify Real‑World Examples
practice.instruction: Look at the three items below and write whether each one is an AI model, an AI tool, or an AI application: 1) A speech‑to‑text engine that converts audio to text. 2) A mobile app that lets you translate spoken words using that engine. 3) The underlying neural network that powers the speech conversion.

keyTakeaways: An AI model is the trained algorithm; it has no user interface.
An AI tool connects a model to a specific task with a simple interface.
An AI application bundles tools, data, and interfaces into a complete product.
Understanding the layers helps avoid confusing a model with the whole product.

mcqs.question: What is the main difference between an AI model and an AI tool?
options: An AI model includes a user interface, while an AI tool does not.
An AI model is a trained algorithm without a user interface; an AI tool connects that model to a user-friendly interface for a specific task.
An AI tool is the raw data used to train the model.
An AI model can be directly used by people without any software.
mcqs.explanation: The lesson states that a model is just the learned algorithm with no UI, whereas a tool adds an interface to let users perform a task.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of an AI application?
options: GPT‑4 language model
Grammarly grammar checker
Adobe Photoshop with Neural Filters
A face‑recognition model used in a phone
mcqs.explanation: Photoshop combines the Neural Filters model with menus, file handling, and other features, making it a complete AI application.

mcqs.question: In the steps that turn a model into a usable product, what typically follows the step of wrapping the model with code that handles inputs and outputs?
options: Training a new model
Designing a user interface or API
Adding data management and security layers
Deploying the model to a cloud server
mcqs.explanation: After the model is wrapped with code, developers usually create a UI or API so users can interact with the system.

mcqs.question: Which statement best describes an AI tool?
options: A program that connects a model to a user‑friendly interface for a specific task.
The raw mathematical representation learned from data.
A complete product that includes storage, security, and integration features.
A dataset used for training the model.
mcqs.explanation: An AI tool is software that links a model to a simple interface, allowing people to perform a particular task.

mcqs.question: According to the lesson, the speech‑to‑text engine is an AI ___, and the mobile app that translates spoken words using that engine is an AI ___.
options: model, tool
tool, application
application, model
model, application
mcqs.explanation: The engine itself is the trained model, while the mobile app that packages the engine with UI and extra features is an AI application.
